boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Marist gatherings and practices, from Welcome Week field games to a campus tree lit with thousands of LEDs.

cards.title: Make Family Weekend a Red Fox reunion
cards.subtitle: Annual Marist tradition · campuswide
cards.notes: Plan around the Friday-through-Sunday program, then use the official schedule to choose family-friendly performances, games, and gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A fall weekend that brings students and their families together on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist identifies Family Weekend as a tradition and says the program runs from Friday evening through Sunday afternoon.
cards.access_notes: Dates and registration details are posted by Student Affairs; some listed activities may have fees.

cards.title: Join Fox Fest’s spring reset
cards.subtitle: Annual spring celebration · campuswide
cards.notes: Watch for the Residence Life schedule and pick an activity, outdoor gathering, or evening program that fits your day on campus.
cards.short_summary: A long-running Residence Life celebration expanded into a full-day campus event in 2026.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist calls Fox Fest its annual spring celebration and a long Residence Life staple becoming a broader spring tradition.
cards.source_title: Fox Fest, Marist’s Annual Spring Celebration, Expands into All-Day Event
cards.access_notes: Programming, timing, and any activity-specific requirements vary by year.

cards.title: Mark the calendar for Spring Concert
cards.subtitle: Annual campus event · Marist University
cards.notes: Check Student Programming Council announcements for the artist, venue, entry rules, and companion events before making plans.
cards.short_summary: The annual concert anchors Marist’s spring campus-life calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist lists the spring concert among annual community gatherings and identifies it as a highly anticipated annual event.
cards.source_title: Student Activities and Clubs — Marist University
cards.access_notes: Artist, date, location, and admission details change annually.

cards.title: See the Holiday Tree come alive
cards.subtitle: Annual ceremony · outside Our Lady Seat of Wisdom Chapel
cards.notes: Bundle up for the lighting and arrive early enough to hear the music and see the campus centerpiece switch on.
cards.short_summary: A holiday gathering centered on Marist’s illuminated campus tree.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist describes the Holiday Tree lighting as an annual event; it says campus tree celebrations date to the 1980s.
cards.source_title: Holiday Celebrations Across Cultures Bring Campus Community Together
cards.access_notes: The ceremony’s date, start time, and program are announced each holiday season.

cards.title: Share a P.S. I Love You message
cards.subtitle: Second Friday in February · Murray Student Center
cards.notes: Visit the student-center tables, take part in the positive-message activities, and use the event’s support resources thoughtfully.
cards.short_summary: An annual Marist observance promoting kindness, mental-health awareness, and suicide prevention.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist calls P.S. I Love You Day its annual tradition of honoring love, kindness, and positivity, held on the second Friday in February.
cards.access_notes: Annual activities are hosted on campus; consult Student Affairs for current participation details.

cards.title: Start with the New Student Welcome
cards.subtitle: Orientation tradition · Marist University
cards.notes: Treat this orientation gathering as your first campus-wide checkpoint, then follow the current schedule for your student group.
cards.short_summary: A formal annual welcome moment for incoming Marist students.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s orientation schedule describes the New Student Welcome as an annual tradition and the moment incoming students are welcomed.
cards.access_notes: Orientation schedules differ by cohort and year; use the current official schedule.

cards.title: Rally at the Red Fox Rumble
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week field-day games · Marist University
cards.notes: Bring comfortable clothes and join the Welcome Week field-day activities when the current first-year schedule announces them.
cards.short_summary: A first-year game tradition that Marist recreated as part of Fox Fest programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist’s Fox Fest coverage identifies the Red Fox Rumble as Welcome Week field day-style games for first-year students.
cards.source_title: Fox Fest, Marist’s Annual Spring Celebration, Expands into All-Day Event
cards.access_notes: Participation details and scheduling are released with Welcome Week programming.

cards.title: Take part in the Giving Tree Project
cards.subtitle: December service tradition · Marist community
cards.notes: Look for the seasonal giving instructions, select a requested item only if you can fulfill it, and follow the posted delivery steps.
cards.short_summary: A December community-giving project coordinated through Marist’s spiritual-life and service work.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist says the Giving Tree Project provides holiday gifts to local families through campus clubs, organizations, offices, and individuals.
cards.access_notes: Participation typically involves donating requested gifts; follow the current project instructions.

cards.title: Turn November into Hunger Awareness Month
cards.subtitle: November service programming · Marist University
cards.notes: Choose a current service, food-collection, or awareness activity and use the official program details to participate responsibly.
cards.short_summary: A November series that combines hunger education, fundraising, and community collection efforts.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist identifies November as Hunger Awareness Month and lists its Walk/Run for Hunger, food collection, meal, and Petition Day activities.
cards.access_notes: Activities and contribution options vary each year; some participation may involve a donation.

cards.title: Use Marist’s first-year mentor tradition
cards.subtitle: First Year Experience · Marist University
cards.notes: Meet your assigned mentor early, bring practical questions, and use their connections to navigate campus resources and organizations.
cards.short_summary: A mentoring practice begun in the late 1970s to help new students transition and succeed.
cards.evidence_claim: Marist says its mentorship tradition began in the late 1970s and that mentors connect first-year students with support and campus life.
cards.access_notes: Available to first-year students through the First Year Experience program.
